To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
training users on an interface that is designed to prevent them from making common errors results in faster and better learning.
a user interface designed to prevent error states can substantially reduce the time required to learn a complex application system and improve learning achievement.
a training environment that eliminates the sources of new-user learning problems can substantially speed up learning, improve learning achievement, and improve comprehension performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to organize function in a way that facilitates learning.
the design of user interfaces that support the learning process.
the design of a user interface that is both easy to learn and easy to use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the training wheels worked.
training wheels in a user-interface can make a difference in learning, but the difference depends upon the nature of the interface and the nature of the task.
the use of a training interface can reduce the amount of time required for users to learn to use a computer application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the training interface was effective because it was designed from the basic functions of the system.
training wheels are not only a good idea, but that the training wheels should be built into the interface itself.
training interfaces should be designed to make error states unreachable, thus eliminating the sources and the time required for new users to make errors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a training interface can be built from the function of a system itself.
the design of the training environment can be a critical factor in the learning process.
training environments should not be created by adding new functions to the basic system.
